name: flags-planted-usability-issues
prompt: Can you usability-test our web shop like real customers would? The main task is buying a tea. Site is in this folder – serve it with `python3 -m http.server 8000`.
assertions: The report shows results for at least the five default personas (power user, keyboard-only, low-confidence, screen-reader or low-vision, mobile on slow connection), e.g. in a task-results line or persona column.
The report flags that the checkout 'Continue' (or payment 'Submit') control is a non-focusable div and cannot be operated by keyboard, citing WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard.
The report flags form fields that have only placeholders and no labels, citing WCAG 1.3.1, 3.3.2 or 4.1.2.
The report flags removed focus outline / no visible focus (WCAG 2.4.7) or low colour contrast text (WCAG 1.4.3).

The report flags at least one of: images or icon links without accessible names/alt text (1.1.1/2.4.4/4.1.2), zoom disabled with user-scalable=no (1.4.4), small touch targets (2.5.8), or errors indicated only by a red border (1.4.1/3.3.1).
Findings are ranked by severity and each finding lists which personas hit it (or a count).
Every finding names its principle: a WCAG 2.2 criterion number, a Nielsen heuristic, or another named law/pattern.
The report opens with a score line of the form 'Passed X of Y' task runs (or checks).

name: no-false-findings-on-clean-site
prompt: We just rebuilt our tea shop with accessibility in mind. Please usability-test it as different kinds of users – main task is buying a tea. It's in this folder (serve with `python3 -m http.server 8000`).
assertions: The report states that all personas completed the purchase task (or no persona was blocked).
The report does not list any finding with severity 3 or 4 (major or catastrophe) or 'high/critical'.
The report does not claim keyboard operation is impossible, that form fields lack labels, or that focus is invisible (all false for this site).
